item.title: Trump criticizes '60 Minutes' bosses as 'even worse' as he challenges Iran war report
item.description: President Donald Trump blasted CBS' "60 Minutes" for omitting U.S. defensive wins against Iranian drones in a report as he lashed out at the news program.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump criticized CBS' "60 Minutes" on Monday, following correspondent Norah O’Donnell’s report on a deadly Iranian attack against American troops in Kuwait — accusing the program of omitting U.S. defensive successes. 

"The new people running 60 Minutes are even worse than their predecessors. A recent study on an attack in the early stages of Iran was not correctly stated," Trump said in a post on Truth Social. 

A CBS insider defended its investigation and pointed to reports of another Iranian drone attack targeting an American base in Bahrain.

"The Truth Social post on U.S. drone capabilities (despite reports of an Iranian drone strike on another US base in Bahrain yesterday) is an attempt to distract from 60 MINUTES’ 8-month investigation that revealed U.S. military failures surrounding the deadliest attack against U.S. troops in the war with Iran," a CBS insider told Fox News Digital.

TRUMP DOUBLES DOWN ON ATTACKS AGAINST 'TERRIBLE' '60 MINUTES' HOST NORAH O'DONNELL

Trump's criticism centered on the program’s treatment of U.S. defenses since Operation Epic Fury began Feb. 28. He cited thousands of Iranian drone launches while defending the military’s performance.

"Since February 28, 2026, the start of Epic Fury, Iran has fired between 8,000-9,000 One-way Attack Drones," Trump said on Truth Social. "Only 2 of them got through, resulting in U.S. fatalities, both on the first day, hitting Kuwait and Saudi Arabia."

The president also cited approximately 2,000 Iranian ballistic missiles and one that caused American fatalities in Jordan. He combined interceptions and attacks that did not cause American deaths in assessing the military's defenses.

"Translation: 99.99% of Iranian missiles and drones have been shot down or, in any event, not caused U.S. deaths. CENTCOM defensive measures have been historically effective. No one in the World has the ability to do so well. All of this being left out of the 60 Minutes 'report,'" Trump said.

The president's criticism of the show was noteworthy as many liberal critics have accused new CBS editor-in-chief Bari Weiss of being too Trump-friendly, despite "60 Minutes" running numerous critical segments under her watch.

ARMY IDS 2 VICTIMS KILLED IN JORDAN AIR BASE ATTACK; TRUMP: IRAN WILL PAY 'MANY TIMES OVER'

Sunday's "60 Minutes" report by O'Donnell was part of what the network called an eight-month investigation into the Iran war. The report says it reveals the "extent of the damage to U.S. positions in the Middle East," a well as the human costs for the loved ones of the 23 U.S. service members killed and 800 wounded in the conflict.

The CBS insider's response focused on alleged decisions preceding the Kuwait strike, including warnings about the installation's vulnerability and its ability to treat wounded soldiers.

"Norah O'Donnell reported that military leadership at the targeted Army post in Kuwait allegedly disregarded threats of Iran kamikaze drone attacks, ignored U.S. intelligence about Port Shuaiba being on Iran’s target list, failed to deliver a counter drone system, and lacked the basic medical capabilities, including an onsite physician," the CBS insider told Fox News Digital. "All of this leading to the vulnerability of an unprotected American base and death of 6 soldiers."

The insider also directed Fox News Digital to its broadcast transcript, which described satellite imagery and video documenting damage to at least 31 American military and diplomatic sites across eight countries.

COST OF IRAN WAR EXPLODES AS TOLL ON US AIR FLEET NEARLY DOUBLES

The Pentagon declined to answer whether the unit received adequate protection, according to the source. That account concerned The Pentagon’s response to CBS' reporting, rather than a response to Trump’s Monday criticism.

The Pentagon previously defended precautions at the installation. In a March post on X responding to CBS News' reporting about the site’s fortifications, Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell disputed the characterization of the command center as a makeshift office space.

"Every possible measure has been taken to safeguard our troops — at every level," Parnell said at the time.

item.title: Trump brings two divided Cabinet heavyweights to China as controversy hangs over high-stakes talks
item.description: President Donald Trump said Scott Bessent and Howard Lutnick hold opposing views on China as both join his high-stakes Asia trip to meet Xi Jinping.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump is bringing two powerful Cabinet officials divided over restrictions on China's access to advanced American AI chips on his high-stakes Asia trip, as controversy over the issue follows them into talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick are both accompanying Trump on the four-day trip despite reports of a dispute over whether to blacklist a company suspected of helping China obtain restricted American AI technology. Trump acknowledged their competing views Monday and suggested Lutnick may have delayed action to avoid worsening relations with Beijing.

"He might have delayed it, but he was doing that because you could have if you didn't delay it. If you didn't do something, you could have a blow up with China. We're having a very good relationship with China right now, and I understand both sides of it, and I'll make a decision. But I understand very well both sides," the president said.

The dispute follows reports that Lutnick resisted efforts to place Singapore-based Megaspeed on a U.S. trade blacklist, despite Trump reportedly supporting action against the company on three occasions this year, according to Axios. Megaspeed has faced allegations that its operations helped Chinese companies gain access to restricted Nvidia chips.

TWO TOP TRUMP CABINET OFFICIALS GO TO WAR OVER CHINA SPY SCANDAL AMID EXPLOSIVE ACCUSATIONS: REPORT

The Commerce Department announced a new rule this week aimed at preventing Chinese companies and other restricted foreign entities from accessing advanced American computing technology through data centers in third countries. The department said the rule was written at the direction of the Treasury Department and National Security Council.

Trump told reporters Monday he is not considering replacing Lutnick, saying "he's done a very good job."

Bessent publicly confirmed Friday that several administration departments had supported adding Megaspeed to the Commerce Department's Entity List, which would restrict the company's access to U.S. technology.

"Treasury, War, USTR, and State — they were in favor of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months, but Commerce has the pen," Bessent said.

The Commerce Department denied Axios' account of a confrontation between Bessent and Lutnick in the White House Situation Room, saying the two officials had no such conversation.

Trump is bringing several of his administration's most powerful officials on the four-day Asia trip, which includes stops in the Philippines and China.

TRUMP TO CONFRONT XI AT HIGH-STAKES SUMMIT OVER CHINA BACKING FOR IRAN, RUSSIA

The delegation includes Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Bessent, Lutnick, White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller, U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer and National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett, among other officials, a White House official confirmed to Fox News Digital.

Trump is expected to meet with world leaders, participate in regional economic and security summits and hold high-stakes talks with Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin, and possibly North Korea leader Kim Jong Un.

The controversy has also drawn attention to Nvidia's leadership. Nvidia announced Thursday that CEO Jensen Huang had resigned following reports about his relationship with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive suspected by U.S. intelligence of spying for China.

Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing and said Sunday that it retained outside counsel to investigate allegations surrounding its operations.

Trump said Monday it has not been confirmed she is a spy.

FEDERAL PROSECUTOR WARNS SEN WARREN OF 'LEGAL CONSEQUENCES' IF RECORDS AREN'T PRESERVED IN TRUMP-LINKED PROBES

Lutnick, the former chairman and CEO of investment firm Cantor Fitzgerald, is one of the wealthiest officials to serve in a presidential administration. A longtime Trump ally, he co-chaired the president's 2024 transition team, and the two have known each other for decades through New York's business and social circles.

Lutnick has also agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 10 amid growing scrutiny of the Commerce Department's handling of Nvidia chip exports to China, CBS News reported.

Sens. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., and Chris Coons, D-Del., jointly called on the administration to preserve records related to Nvidia's advanced AI chip exports and potential national security risks. The senators set a Nov. 17 deadline for written confirmation that the records would be preserved and requested a congressional briefing.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Fox News Digital reached out to the Departments of Commerce and Treasury for comment.

item.title: Ty Jerome's absence looms large as Grizzlies visit Wizards and 76ers take on Nets in NBA action
item.description: Joel Embiid is a game-time decision as the Philadelphia 76ers visit the Brooklyn Nets, with the under 226.5 favored in a matchup of bottom-half offenses.
item.content:encoded:
The NBA is already about 20% complete, which is almost crazy to think about. The NBA Cup has had some real traction, and we've had some fun surprises in the early season. There are some teams I'm wondering about - will they keep their hot start going, and will others turn it around? I have two different looks for tonight and think both should cash for us.

The Philadelphia 76ers are one of the teams that have put together a hot start, but I don't think anyone really should be surprised. They have a strong group of players in their starting lineup. The big question is whether they can compete with and beat the best teams in the league. How will they manage playing against the Nuggets, Cavs, Knicks, Spurs, and other squads in a seven-game series? Also, health will always be an issue. Joel Embiid hurt himself again recently, and he is a game-time decision in this one.

The Brooklyn Nets are terrible this season, something that also should've been expected. They are 3-9 for the season and just 1-3 in the Barclays Center. Their team is figuring things out to a certain extent. Michael Porter Jr. remains their best scoring option, but just because he can put the ball in the bucket doesn't mean he can translate that into wins for his squad. Julius Randle has always been mostly an isolation player, and finding the right fit for him and players around him has always been a bit of a challenge.

Neither of these teams are scoring a ton of points this year. The 76ers average just 112.6 points per game, and the Nets are at just 110.2. Both are in the bottom half of the league. Defensively, the 76ers are ranked 9th in the league. Brooklyn is 21st. Philadelphia is coming off a home stand and played yesterday. The Nets are coming off a road trip, but do have a bit of a rest advantage. I lean toward Philly covering the -5.5. However, I'm taking the under 226.5 here, as I think both teams coming into Brooklyn for the game will struggle with scoring.

The Memphis Grizzlies have been one of the bigger surprises of this season; the team is 9-4 for the season and hasn't lost a road game this year. Memphis being good wasn't something I expected, and most of it should be attributed to Ty Jerome looking like an All-Star this season. Jerome has averaged 25.4 points per game. Cam Boozer has transitioned well to the NBA game and is averaging almost a double-double for the team.

The Washington Wizards are a team that has struggled to find their footing. This is a bit surprising to me, as their roster is actually pretty deep. They have more than enough pieces to be good; they just aren't. Anthony Davis looks good; Trae Young is averaging about nine assists and 18 points per game. I'm looking forward to seeing how AJ Dybantsa evolves. He is averaging 15.1 points and six rebounds per game.

Jerome will be out for this game, and he is the only player averaging 20 or more points this season for the team. The Wizards are at home and have the better players, but they've also lost seven straight games. They've been at home for two straight games already and did play yesterday, making this the third in four nights, but they were embarrassed by the Rockets. I think they will come in motivated for this one. I like the Wizards to win the game, but feel free to take the +3.5 points if you want. I just don't see the Grizzlies doing this against the Wizards without Jerome on the road. I think Washington wins this one, and I'll put a few units on this.

item.title: Cowboys defensive coordinator shows why he should be fired by asking Von Miller to cover Christian McCaffrey
item.description: The Dallas Cowboys asked Von Miller to cover Christian McCaffrey man-to-man on a cover zero blitz, and the 66-yard touchdown exposed a coaching flaw.
item.content:encoded:
By now everyone understands the Dallas Cowboys defense is, being professional here, horrible, terrible, awful, dreadful.

And the one or two people left on Earth arguing otherwise can go look at one play that makes the case.

The play came during the Cowboys' loss to the San Francisco 49ers in which the defense yielded 46 points and 584 yards and left pundits everywhere calling for the firing of Dallas defensive coordinator Christian Parker.

COWBOYS' ELIJAH GARCIA GETS COMPLETELY FOOLED ON 49ERS' TRICK PLAY, UNDERSCORING POOR DEFENSIVE EFFORT IN LOSS

The play is not the one in which Cowboys defenders ran the wrong way, chasing offensive players that didn't have the football. It's not the one where San Francisco's end around faked out all but one guy on the Dallas defense.

Those are all physical problems. The players either couldn't get there or didn't want to get to the tackle.

The play that speaks mostly to the Dallas problems, meanwhile, is evidence of a coaching problem.

It was a 66-yard touchdown pass from Niners' quarterback Brock Purdy to running back Christian McCaffrey in which Parker asked Von Miller to cover the running back on the play.

VON MILLER SIGNS WITH COWBOYS IN HOMECOMING MOVE FOR 2-TIME SUPER BOWL CHAMPION: 'LET'S MAKE THIS ONE SPECIAL'

Miller, by the way, is an accomplished NFL pass rusher. He has 139.5 sacks in his career, which makes him a Hall of Fame candidate when he's done playing.

But he's not a coverage linebacker. In fact, he's allowed 100 percent of the passes he's been asked to defend to be completed in three of the past four seasons.

And did we mention, he's 37 years old?

But the Cowboys somehow decided that asking their accomplished pass rusher not rush the passer and do what he's not good at, which is get in coverage, at age 37 years old, to cover one of the NFL's best pass-catching running backs, was a good idea.

The play-call by Parker was a blitz.

"Yes, it was cover zero," head coach Brian Schottenheimer admitted afterward. "All-out blitz."

That means Miller had no help on the play. He had to cover man-to-man and the result was the 49ers scoring the points that ultimately decided this game.

COWBOYS COACH BRIAN SCHOTTENHEIMER DEFENDS PLAYERS-ONLY MEETING DESPITE MIKE TOMLIN'S CRITICISM

"Again, it's one of the situations [Parker] went with a call that he liked," Schottenheimer said, "and we got to look at it, but at the end of the day it didn't work out very well for us."

Did Schottenheimer like the call?

"I want to see the film," he said.

That answer might be intended to protect his defensive coaches, particularly Parker. But too late, because the play laid bare how poorly thought-out their call was.

It's not that a zero blitz is a bad call.

It's that a zero blitz that doesn't consider the personnel on the field – in this case having Miller on the field to chase the much younger, much faster McCaffrey – is nonsensical. It glows in neon as a bad matchup.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Any defensive coach who believes an opponent quarterback won't immediately go to his favorite receiver to take advantage of the matchup is simply not very good at playing chess because his move exposes his piece (Miller) to embarrassment.

This, in short, is bad coaching.

The Dallas Cowboys have a lot of issues with their defense. The Cowboys allow more yards per game than any other team and are third-worst in points allowed. And the snapshot of Von Miller chasing Christian McCaffrey on a 66-yard touchdown pass makes that point in living color.

item.title: Titans kicker Joey Slye may have delivered the hardest hit of NFL Week 10 action against Jaguars
item.description: Tennessee Titans kicker Joey Slye delivered a crushing open-field hit that forced a Josh Cameron fumble in the Week 10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars.
item.content:encoded:
With the Tennessee Titans sitting at 1-8 on the season, the franchise has accumulated more lowlights than highlights in 2026, but every now and again, they give their desperate fanbase a reason for excitement. During Tennessee's 40-23 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 10, that excitement came from none other than Titans kicker Joey Slye.

While Slye was a perfect 3-for-3 on field goal attempts against the Jags, one of the most memorable moments from the entire contest had nothing to do with a field goal, or even Slye's leg, but instead his ability to make an open-field tackle.

After connecting on a 54-yard field goal to cut Jacksonville's lead to 16-13 in the early stages of the third quarter, Slye took to his kickoff duties and proceeded to show off his hit stick.

item.title: Justin Herbert's 11 interceptions in eight games highlight the Chargers' disastrous 0-win season
item.description: The winless Los Angeles Chargers meet the 4-5 Baltimore Ravens on a short week, with Justin Herbert's 11 interceptions in eight games fueling a slump.
item.content:encoded:
It was an odd week of football for Week 10, but we aren't quite over yet. I am 1-3 on the week, and looking to at least cut that deficit tonight with a win. I lost on Thursday Night Football as the Commanders beat the Giants. Yesterday, I was wrong about both Kirk Cousins and Fernando Mendoza. Mendoza wasn't terrible, but couldn't get the Raiders quite close enough to cover the spread. Cousins looked great, and the Vikings' defense seemed rejuvenated because they finally had a quarterback. The Bengals and Steelers racked up points, giving me a win in that game. Tonight, I search for a win in what might be the worst match up of the week as the Chargers play the Ravens.

The Los Angeles Chargers are the only team in football that hasn't gotten a win this season. I have to imagine that the line on that wager would've been quite high. This is a team that made the postseason last year. A team that has a strong head coach, a quarterback most felt would be a franchise-level quarterback, and they even added an offensive coordinator who was a head coach and made the Miami Dolphins at least competitive for multiple seasons. So, why is this season such a disaster?

Well, for one thing, Justin Herbert looks awful this season. He has thrown for just 1,591 yards, six touchdowns, and 11 interceptions. For context, Herbert has 11 interceptions in eight games. His yards rank 23rd in the league, and Caleb Williams, Jayden Daniels, and Sam Darnold are all about 100 yards behind him and have played at least one fewer game. As a team, they are getting a reasonable amount of yards per game, but they are dead last in points scored per game at 15.1.

The Baltimore Ravens aren't exactly having a fantastic season themselves. As usual, Lamar Jackson being injured has prevented them from being successful. They are 4-5 for the season, and Jackson has only been available in five games. In his most recent game, he had one attempt and was injured on the play. Then Tyler Huntley came in and was injured. Joe Fagnano took over for the team and looked like what you would expect a third-string quarterback to look.

The team has plenty of weapons still. Zay Flowers is a solid receiver, Mark Andrews is a good tight end, and Derrick Henry remains one of the best running backs in football. They are only averaging 21 points per game, though. Thanks to a trade for Jacoby Brissett, the team at least has a somewhat competent quarterback under center tonight. It will depend on how quickly the team can get him up to speed on the playbook and how quickly he can develop some rapport with them.

RAVENS FINALLY REVEAL LAMAR JACKSON'S OFFICIAL RETURN TIMELINE AND QB COULD MISS REST OF REGULAR SEASON

The Chargers are somewhat healthy, but they are missing Ladd McConkey tonight, so there will be some issues there. McConkey is their best receiver, and missing him will hurt an already terrible passing game. The Ravens don't have a great passing defense, but they should be good enough to stop this one. I think the Ravens should win this with Brissett under center, and I don't think it will be particularly close. I'll take them to cover the -4.5, and I also have a lean to the under 39.5.

item.title: Elderly homeowner’s hired help turns into squatter nightmare made worse by blue state laws: report
item.description: Jordy Smith, 76, said a fake plumber locked her out of her San Diego home and rented rooms to over a dozen people before Squatter Squad intervened.
item.content:encoded:
An elderly woman said a man posing as a plumber took over her home in California and began renting it out to more than a dozen people – many of them appearing to be homeless.

The situation had been brewing for more than two years before law enforcement finally removed the group after blue state laws complicated the issue, according to the homeowner and those helping her.

Jordy Smith, 76, opened up about the situation that took over her life in the City Heights neighborhood of San Diego, where she reportedly hired this man to repair pipes.

He then allegedly locked her out of the home and was renting it out to a revolving door of people, according to KGTV.

ALLEGED MALIBU SERIAL SQUATTER FEATURED IN NEW DOCUSERIES AFTER YEARS OF HOMEOWNER COMPLAINTS

Smith told a reporter that she temporarily moved from her home after she broke a hip and invited the unnamed "plumber" to make the repairs while she was gone.

"He just took over and, like, before we knew it, there was like 15 people," she said.

HOW THE 'SQUATTER HUNTER' IS FIGHTING HOME TAKEOVERS WITH TECH

In a post on social media, Squatter Squad, which is a "squatter removal and prevention" company that was hired to remove the group, said, "Boats were showing up. RVs were moving onto the property. More people were staying there. The contractor had started inviting others onto the property, renting out rooms and even charging people for RV space."

Smith said she later discovered the man was not a licensed plumber and had transferred the home’s utility accounts into his name before allegedly beginning to rent out rooms to others.

NYC LANDLORD PLEADS FOR HELP AS '9-YEAR-SQUATTER' CONTINUES TO DRAIN HIM DRY IN COURT SAGA: 'TWILIGHT ZONE'

She and her partner found themselves locked out of their own home.

"I couldn’t sleep at night. I mean, it just seemed like we’d never get back home," she said.

SAN FRANCISCO HOME WITH HISTORY OF SQUATTERS UNDER CONTRACT FOR $1.3 MILLION

Attempts to confront the people living inside reportedly went nowhere, with Smith saying occupants would lock the door and refuse to speak with them.

Squatter Squad told KGTV that squatter issues are "often treated as civil matters," making it difficult for homeowners to remove them.

LEE GILLEY BEGS FOR ITALIAN PROTECTION AS ALLEGED SQUATTER TARGETS HOME WHERE PREGNANT WIFE WAS KILLED

Under California law, if squatters continuously reside on a property for 30 days, they legally acquire "tenant-at-will" rights.

SUPREME COURT REJECTS MICHIGAN FAMILY'S CLAIM THAT COUNTY COMMITTED 'HOME EQUITY THEFT' OVER $2,200 TAX DEBT

Once this 30-day threshold is reached, law enforcement treats the situation as a civil landlord-tenant matter rather than criminal trespassing, meaning police cannot simply remove the occupant, and the property owner must go through the formal legal eviction process to regain possession.

In a statement sent to Fox News Digital, Lando Thomas, owner of Squatter Squad, said:

"California’s tenant protection laws serve an important purpose, but they can also create unintended challenges when individuals unlawfully occupy properties. In some situations, the legal framework makes it difficult for law enforcement to quickly distinguish between legitimate tenants and individuals who have no lawful right to occupy a property. When that distinction cannot be established immediately, property owners may be forced into lengthy and costly legal proceedings to regain possession of their own property.

"The issue isn’t whether legitimate tenants deserve protection. They absolutely do. The issue is ensuring that those protections cannot be exploited by individuals who unlawfully occupy someone else’s property. We need a system that protects legitimate tenants while also providing property owners and law enforcement with a clear, efficient process for addressing unlawful occupancy."

Squatter Squad shared a video showing deputies from the San Diego County Sheriff's Office confronting the squatters in August.

"We worked with the local sheriff’s department and followed the legal process. It took time. It even required an eviction. But in the end, we got the property back," Squatter Squad said.

As for the homeowner – she is pleading with her state to make changes to stop this situation from happening.

item.title: Leon Slater retains TNA world title at Destination X after Trey Miguel's resilience amid travel chaos
item.description: Leon Slater retained the TNA World Championship at Destination X after a bloody battle with Trey Miguel, who nearly missed the Edmonton show.
item.content:encoded:
In pro wrestling, sometimes the destination isn’t the story – it’s how you got there.

Trey Miguel was among those in the industry who had to go through one hell of a journey to get to a show over the weekend. Questions surrounded him about whether he would actually show up at Total Nonstop Action Wrestling’s (TNA) Destination X pay-per-view on Sunday night.

Miguel followed through and made it to the Edmonton Expo Centre in Edmonton, Alberta, Canada, despite the travel chaos that hampered millions of people across North America since Friday. He wasn’t about to miss one of his first chances to win the TNA World Championship.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE

The only thing stopping him in the arena was defending champion Leon Slater.

Slater looked and felt like the champion throughout the match. It was his first title defense since he won the championship back at Bound for Glory. Miguel proved to be a formidable challenger despite the hours of traveling and the lack of proper preparation to get ready for the match.

A Styles Clash led Slater to a second attempt at the Swanton 450 from the top rope. Before he could perform the move, Miguel hit him with an uppercut. Slater caught Miguel, who was trying to go for a hurricanrana. Miguel shimmied his way down Slater’s body and connected. The match went to the outside of the ring as a frustrated Slater looked to finally put Miguel away. Miguel landed onto the steel steps and was busted open.

Slater had to go to the deepest parts of himself to put Miguel away. Miguel wouldn’t quit. Blow after blow and headshot after headshot wore Miguel down. Slater hit Utopia on Miguel and demanded the referee count to three. Miguel still wouldn’t be put away. Somehow, something ignited in Miguel and tried to get a quick roll up on Slater but to no avail.

Miguel got some breathing room when he dropped Slater onto an exposed part of the turnbuckle. It busted open Slater. Miguel nailed Slater with a meteroa from the top turnbuckle onto Slater on the apron. Miguel clutched his knee as Slater got back into the ring.

"Fight forever" chants began to ring out in the arena. Each man was bringing out all they had for the epic main event. A series of blocked suplexes landed both men outside the ring. Miguel hit a Lighting Spiral on Slater and both men went down.

Miguel hit a meteroa from the top rope but Slater countered it into a submission maneuver. Miguel found a way out of it. Slater avoided another meteroa attempt and met Miguel with a thrust kick.

Slater hit the Swanton 450 and pinned Miguel for the win.

Slater is the youngest world champion in TNA’s history. He still managed to keep it that way after a terrific match against Miguel.

Miguel deserved every bit of praise for getting to Edmonton for the match. He could have backed out and stayed home, but his desire to be a world champion carried him across the border. The only issue is that he ran into Slater.

The Ultimate X match is one of the cornerstone features in TNA’s history. Though the initial card was altered, six men showed up and put on a great match.

Joe Alonzo, KC Navarro, John Skyler and Cedric Alexander were initially announced as the participants after travel chaos affected the card. A.J. Francis put himself in the match during the pre-show. TNA Director of Authority Santino Marella added TJP to the mix before the match started.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The match came down to who wanted it more. Navarro, at one point, thought Francis had a change of heart. Navarro sat on Francis’ shoulders as the former First Class teammates and climbed the cable to try to grab the X. Francis decided his help wasn’t needed anymore and hit Navarro with a TFL as he clung to the cable.

Francis had his own shot to grab the X – twice. The first time, Alexander powerbombed him to the canvas. Then, as Navarro grabbed the X, Francis had him in position to steal the item away from him. But Navarro unhooked the X and caught it before falling to the canvas.

Navarro will now get a shot at the X Division Championship against Amazing Red down the line.

The Knockouts Ultimate X match made its debut in TNA back in 2022 at Hard to Kill. It was Tasha Steelz who won that match in January 2022. More than four years later, Steelz again proved she was more than worthy of capturing the Knockouts Championship.

Steelz, with the help of tag team partner Kiera Hogan, climbed the top turnbuckle and inched her way to the X above the middle of the ring. Hogan played defense with a kendo stick to allow Steelz to grab the token.

She will face Indi Hartwell for the TNA Knockouts Championship somewhere down the line, possibly after Shayna Baszler gets her shot. Baszler was set to challenge Hartwell for the title on the card, but the champion was unable to make it to Edmonton due to travel issues.

Meanwhile, The Elegance Brand appeared to have some more issues.

Heather by Elegance put on a show as she moonsaulted off a truss to knockout her opponents. It was far from enough to win the match. M by Elegance, the Knockouts TV champion, tried her best to get the X. She kinda, sorta helped Heather attempt to grab it but to no avail.

M then tried to grab the X for herself as Baszler was choking out Heather.

It appeared a major rift was cracking through the Elegance Brand.

item.title: Trump leaves door open to Kim Jong Un joining high-stakes talks with Xi, Putin
item.description: Trump suggested Kim Jong Un could appear during his China trip, saying the North Korean leader's presence is up to Xi Jinping ahead of trilateral talks in China.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump offered a brief, unexpected response about North Korea during a White House gaggle Monday, adding a new wrinkle to his closely watched trip to Asia this week.

Trump suggested North Korean leader Kim Jong Un could make an appearance during his China trip, telling reporters, "We might have Kim Jong Un. He may come, I don’t know. That’s up to President Xi."

The comment came in response to a reporter's question about the upcoming high-stakes meetings between Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin at the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, China, and whether the trio planned to discuss North Korean nuclear capabilities.

PRESIDENT TRUMP TO HOLD HISTORIC TRILATERAL SUMMIT WITH XI AND PUTIN

Trump and Kim last met in 2019, when their Hanoi summit ended without an agreement on North Korea’s nuclear program. Nonetheless, Pyongyang has since expanded its nuclear and missile capabilities, while efforts to restart talks have stalled. In August, Trump said he expected to meet Kim "later this year," but North Korea pushed back, with Kim Yo Jong saying the leaders’ relationship remained "excellent" while accusing Washington of maintaining hostile policies toward Pyongyang, Fox News Digital reported at the time.

Meanwhile, a U.S. official said last week, according to ABC News, that there were no plans for North Korea engagement during Trump’s Asia trip, and experts say the country is unlikely to feature prominently in the trilateral talks.

South Korean news outlet Yonhap News Agency reported Monday that South Korea’s Foreign Ministry said it hoped high-level talks on the sidelines of the APEC summit would contribute to peace and stability on the Korean Peninsula. South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun reportedly raised the possibility of renewed U.S.-North Korea dialogue at the summit with his Chinese counterpart, Wang Yi, in Beijing on Friday, stressing that South Korea has vital interests in Korean Peninsula issues and hopes that its perspective is taken into account.

NORTH KOREA MISSILE COULD PUT GUAM IN RANGE AS KIM REBUFFS TRUMP OUTREACH: EXPERT

The South Korean news agency also reported Monday that Andrew Yeo, a senior fellow at the U.S.-based Brookings Institution, said North Korea’s nuclear program is unlikely to be discussed at the summit, citing differences between Washington and Moscow over Pyongyang’s nuclear ambitions. The report also highlighted comments from Korea Economic Institute senior fellow Ellen Kim, who reportedly suggested the leaders could briefly discuss North Korea behind closed doors, but nuclear arms control and the war in Iran are likely to take priority. Ellen Kim added that Xi or Putin could relay a message from Trump to Kim Jong Un, though they may be reluctant to support U.S.-North Korea negotiations for fear of losing influence over Pyongyang.

The trilateral meeting is scheduled for 2:30 p.m. Thursday local time at Shenzhen Kylin Villa, according to Trump’s public schedule.

White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales said Friday that Trump planned to discuss nuclear arms reduction with Xi and Putin, while a senior U.S. official said Iran would also be on the agenda. The Associated Press reported Monday that Trump plans to raise Russia’s war in Ukraine at the meeting as well.

Asked Monday what it would take for Putin to back down from the war in Ukraine, Trump said he thinks Putin "is backing down a little bit."

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

"I think he's backing down a little bit. I think he could be tougher," Trump told reporters Monday outside the White House. "I think it could be a lot tougher, frankly."

Fox News Digital has reached out to the White House for additional comment.

item.title: Fetterman's Gaza-born challenger calls to 'abolish ICE,' oust top Democratic leaders
item.description: Gaza-born socialist Ahmed Moor challenged one of Israel's strongest Senate supporters while calling for an overhaul of Democratic leadership.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: It’s a circumstance almost ripped from a screenplay: a Gaza-born political newcomer wants to topple one of the Senate’s staunchest supporters of Israel in the Democratic Party.

But for Ahmed Moor, a member of the Democratic Socialists of America who is the first to toss his hat into the arena to challenge Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., the story doesn't end there.

"Look, so this race is not about John Fetterman," Moor told Fox News Digital in an interview. "John Fetterman's story is over, but the story of the United States continues. I'm getting in now because I believe we're in the midst of a constitutional crisis."

GAZA-BORN DEMOCRATIC SOCIALIST LAUNCHES PRIMARY BID AGAINST SEN JOHN FETTERMAN

"I have some compassion for John Fetterman — I want to depersonalize," he continued. "Let's talk about policy. The policies that man has expressed and committed to are just a reflection of the special interests which have run his office for too long now. The problem of John Fetterman's policies is the problem of corruption in America."

Fetterman is up for re-election in the 2028 cycle and has become a target for Democrats in Pennsylvania ready to replace him as he continuously moved more to the center of the political spectrum and aligned with Republicans on key issues like the war in Iran, government funding and immigration.

Whether he runs again for a second term remains in the air. When asked by Fox News Digital if he had made a decision, Fetterman said, "The more, the merrier," to challengers entering the Democratic primary.

But Moor, so far, is the only candidate officially in the race.

FETTERMAN WARNS THERE IS NO LONGER 'COMMON GROUND' WITH FAR-LEFT DEMOCRATS OVER ISRAEL

"I know, he seems to really love Hamas," Fetterman said. "And now, so, like, so if you tell him, say thank you for running."

Moor was born in Gaza before immigrating to Philadelphia, where he went to public schools, attended the University of Pennsylvania and later went to Harvard to obtain a public policy degree.

His policy positions are in line with the growing progressive flank in the Senate Democratic caucus and echo the positions that Fetterman first ran on in 2022 when he pledged to support the Senate’s progressive standard-bearer, Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., if he won.

"I spent a lot of time on international policy, kind of a foreign policy specialist, one of the reasons the Senate job appeals to me," Moor said. "But equally, I'm committed to what I call the ‘Dignity Agenda,’ which is universal access to healthcare, childcare and affordable housing."

Among the top concerns for Moor in the "constitutional crisis" he sees in the country is freedom of speech, which he contended came under assault during the Biden administration when protests against "the genocide in Palestine" exploded across college campuses.

FETTERMAN PLAYS POLITICAL MAVERICK, BUT HIS VOTING RECORD TELLS ANOTHER STORY

"Students were brutalized for assembly, for speech," Moor said. "That shouldn't happen in America. Donald Trump stepped through that breach and accelerated the assault. And ICE today is the worst expression, the violation of due process in America."

Like other Democrats and progressives, Moor wants to abolish Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), but he would "like to see immigration law enforced."

"ICE is a lawless organization — ICE is a paramilitary militia. ICE is not law enforcement," he said. "Let's abolish ICE. Let's hold the bad actors who've killed Americans and kidnapped others in our streets. Let's hold them to account for breaking our local ordinance and our local laws. That's a criminal matter today in America. I hope local prosecutors run with it."

And like other progressives who scored stunning victories during the midterm elections to help flip the Senate, like Sens.-elect Abdul El-Sayed and Peggy Flanagan, Moor is against the old guard of Democratic leadership staying in charge.

It’s a position that is gaining steam in the Senate, where Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., is mounting a rare challenge to Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., to lead Democrats through the forthcoming majority in the upper chamber.

Moor said Schumer and House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., both have to go.

"Chuck Schumer and Hakeem Jeffries don't have what it takes to meet the moment. They need to be replaced," Moor said. "This campaign is also about sustaining pressure in that direction. If they survive the leadership contest, which is underway today, I'm going to continue to sustain the pressure on both of those men to do the right thing continuously."

item.title: OpenAI child safety tools target AI-generated abuse
item.description: OpenAI's new classifier flags 48% fewer images for review while detecting similar levels of CSAM, and ChatGPT now suspends users for 24 hours.
item.content:encoded:
A teenager posts a perfectly innocent photo online. Before long, someone uses artificial intelligence to turn it into a sexually explicit fake and shares it with classmates. It's disturbing to think that something as simple as sharing a photo could lead to this kind of abuse. And for the child involved, the damage can last long after the fake picture gets taken down.

Now OpenAI is stepping up its efforts to tackle the problem. The company is introducing a new AI tool designed to detect suspected child sexual abuse material, including content created with artificial intelligence. It's also cracking down on attempts to find abusive material through ChatGPT, with new warnings and 24-hour suspensions. Here's a closer look at what's changing and what parents need to know.

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.

Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

ROBLOX SHARES AI CHILD-SAFETY TOOLS PARENTS SHOULD KNOW

Finding child sexual abuse material online has become more complicated as AI-generated content spreads. Many existing detection systems use digital fingerprints, called hashes, to recognize previously identified abusive files. However, newly created material may have no matching fingerprint. OpenAI's new classifier examines visual signs of potential child sexual abuse material, also known as CSAM. That allows it to flag suspected abuse even when the content has never been identified before.

The system assigns scores to potentially abusive pictures so human reviewers can decide which cases need attention first. OpenAI says it developed and evaluated the technology with help from the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC) at missingkids.org/. The company is offering the classifier at no cost to vetted organizations through its API. That could give smaller child protection teams access to detection technology they otherwise couldn't afford.

OpenAI says its early testing produced encouraging results. In an evaluation involving pictures uploaded to its systems, the company compared the new classifier with its existing protections. The findings suggest the new tool could flag 48% fewer pictures for review while detecting roughly the same amount of abusive material. Pictures flagged by the new classifier were also about twice as likely to contain abuse.

Outside organizations reported additional results. AI platform Fal said its reviewers confirmed 72% of high-confidence flags as previously unidentified CSAM. Meanwhile, SafetyKit reported that the classifier detected 90% of cases involving drawings or animations that sexualize children in its evaluation. These results come from OpenAI and participating organizations. Independent testing will help determine how reliably the technology performs across different platforms.

INSTAGRAM'S AI MAY CATCH TEENS LYING ABOUT THEIR AGE

OpenAI is also changing how ChatGPT responds when someone attempts to find child sexual abuse material. New warnings will interrupt those attempts and explain the harm caused by sexualizing children. The warnings specifically address AI-generated material, which can cause serious harm even when a picture has been digitally fabricated. Along with displaying a warning, OpenAI says it will remove the flagged conversation and pause access to ChatGPT for 24 hours. The warning will also direct the person toward specialist support designed to help prevent harmful behavior.

Repeated violations may lead to longer restrictions or permanent account closure. OpenAI says they could also result in reports to authorities. The new warnings focus on attempts to find abusive material. Under its existing policies, OpenAI says it bans accounts and reports attempts to generate or upload CSAM to NCMEC. The company developed the warnings with input from child protection organizations and researchers who study ways to interrupt harmful online behavior. However, whether these interventions prevent future abuse will require continued evaluation.

OpenAI is expanding its work with organizations investigating online child exploitation. The company says it has begun participating in the Tech Coalition's Lantern program, which allows organizations to share information about suspected exploitation across platforms. It's also introducing specialized AI tools and training for child safety law enforcement units. The first investigative tool will help authorized teams review lengthy chat logs and records obtained through legal processes. Investigators can use it to identify potential connections and organize timelines, with findings linked to source material. Access will depend on agency authorization and program requirements. OpenAI is also publishing guidance to help developers detect suspected abuse and establish procedures for reviewing potentially harmful content.

IS CYBERBULLYING HIDING IN YOUR CHILD'S GROUP CHAT?

You can't control every way someone might misuse a child's photo. However, a few steps can help families reduce exposure and respond if something happens.

Most importantly, make sure children know they can come to you without automatically losing access to their devices. That conversation may help them speak up before harmful content spreads further.

HAWLEY CHAMPIONS GUARD ACT AS HEARTBROKEN FAMILIES SAY AI CHATBOTS ALLEGEDLY PUSHED TEENS TO SELF-HARM

If you're a parent or grandparent, these developments could help improve protection against AI-generated child sexual abuse material. However, the new classifier works behind the scenes. Its impact will depend on how widely organizations adopt it and how effectively their safety teams respond to warnings.

The scale of the problem is alarming. According to NCMEC, its CyberTipline received more than 400,000 reports involving generative AI in 2025. These reports cover several categories of AI-related child exploitation, although not all involved the creation or sharing of AI-generated abuse material.

I'm glad to see OpenAI making this detection technology available to vetted organizations for free. The early results are encouraging, especially if investigators can spend less time reviewing false alarms and more time identifying children who need help. I also support putting consequences behind ChatGPT's warnings. A 24-hour suspension sends a stronger message than simply telling someone their request violates the rules. We've already seen how AI-generated content can be used to harm children, and technology companies need to stay ahead of those who misuse their tools. item.title: WWE's Charlotte Flair reflects on Royal Rumble wins ahead of 2027 event, feels 'pressure' after making history
item.description: Charlotte Flair reveals the emotional pressure of being WWE's only two-time women's Royal Rumble winner ahead of the 2027 event in Glendale, Arizona.
item.content:encoded:
Charlotte Flair has accrued an impressive list of accolades during her time in WWE. She’s a 14-time world champion, a Triple Crown champion and a Grand Slam champion.

What is arguably more impressive than those feats is that she is the one and only two-time women’s Royal Rumble winner. She won the match in 2020 and defeated Rhea Ripley at WrestleMania 36 for the NXT Women’s Championship. In 2025, she won after coming all the way back from a devastating injury but fell short of capturing the title against Tiffany Stratton at WrestleMania 41.

"The first Royal Rumble that I won in Houston, it definitely was a ‘this is my division’ (moment)," Flair told OutKick Dropkick in a recent interview. "I actually could not believe I won. It was such a surreal moment. I felt it in all my being.

"But when I came back the second time in 2025, after my knee injury, I very much was a shell of myself. Hadn't been in the ring in a year, year and a half. Were people gonna remember ‘The Queen?’ Even with my accolades, ‘cause I always think, you know, you're just as good as your last match. So, I was very nervous. Wasn't sure what the reception was gonna be, but knowing that I had crossed the finish lines in terms of when I was away, being back in that ring was all that I thought about. So, all that preparation to get back and how hard it was to get back to me on a professional and personal level meant the world to me."

The Royal Rumble will take place on Feb. 6, 2027, at State Farm Stadium in Glendale, Arizona. It’s the 40th annual event and it will be the 10th edition for the women of the WWE roster. Tickets for the premium live event will go on sale Wednesday.

Flair said she is feeling the pressure since she’s won the match twice already.

"For me, I feel like because I have won two, there's even more pressure. First woman to win two, are the odds forever in my favor? Could I win three? But also in the Rumble, it's always past, present, future. I'm looking forward to seeing which NXT stars come up and make their debut in the Rumble. I think that's always so exciting, and who's gonna show up, show out, make a name for themselves, it's an opportunity.

"But also, Royal Rumble is so important because it gives two people the opportunity to punch their ticket to WrestleMania, which is our biggest show of the year, guaranteeing title match opportunities, and to me it doesn't get any bigger in our business than holding the WWE championship."

Flair, who’s the daughter of pro wrestling legend Ric Flair, recalled some of her favorite moments she’s seen outside of her own victories.

Ric Flair won the 1992 Royal Rumble from the No. 3 spot. Charlotte conceded it was one of her top moments.

"I know this is a lame answer, but when my dad won the Rumble from the three spot, with the ‘a tear in my eye’ promo, will forever be such an iconic Rumble win, in my opinion, and it's not just 'cause he's my dad."

item.title: Seattle mayor orders park named for American president renamed
item.description: Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson ordered Jackson Park renamed, citing Andrew Jackson's legacy of forcibly displacing Native American peoples from their lands.
item.content:encoded:
Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson has ordered a city park named after President Andrew Jackson to be renamed to better fit "the values of our city."

The city argues that Jackson's legacy includes policies that forcibly displaced Native American peoples from their ancestral lands. Wilson directed the Seattle Parks and Recreation to begin a community renaming process on Monday. The 160-acre Jackson Park plays host to the Jackson Park Golf Course.

"We’ve heard from community members who want to change the name of Jackson Park, and now is the right time to move this conversation forward. With new light rail connections and opportunities to make the park more accessible and welcoming, we should have a park that reflects the values of our city," Wilson said in a statement.

WASHINGTON AG'S OFFICE INDICATES IT WILL DEFEND GIRLS' SPORTS BALLOT MEASURE AFTER ACLU SUES TO BLOCK IT

"I’m directing Seattle Parks and Recreation to begin a community naming process to find a name that better reflects this place, its history, and the people who enjoy it," she added.

The renaming effort comes just days after Wilson also backed an effort to block a girls sports initiative that overwhelmingly passed a statewide vote.

SEATTLE MAYOR BACKS EFFORT TO BLOCK GIRLS' SPORTS INITIATIVE THAT PASSED IN 36 OF WASHINGTON'S 39 COUNTIES

Wilson said last week that she supports the Seattle School Board's unanimous vote to pursue legal action against Initiative 638 — which would enforce separation of boys and girls in K-12 sports in Washington state.

Voters passed the measure by a 13-point margin last week, and it won in 36 of the Evergreen State's 39 counties. But after deliberating behind closed doors Monday, the Seattle School Board voted publicly to authorize potential legal action against the measure without hearing public testimony.

"Last night, the Seattle Public Schools Board of Directors voted to authorize legal action regarding Initiative 638. The Board's decision reflects concerns shared by educators, families, community leaders, and the City of Seattle about the measure's impact on student privacy, safety, dignity, and equitable access to educational opportunities," Wilson said in a statement last week.

Fox News' Matt Calkins contributed to this report.

item.title: After the blue wave, what happens to education policy and parental rights protections in flipped states?
item.description: Democratic governors in previously red states look to target school vouchers and change education policies as they come to power next year.
item.content:encoded:
Democrats' sweeping midterm victories in several key governor's races could usher in a new era for education policy, raising urgent questions about the future of the parental rights laws Republicans spent years cementing after the COVID-19 pandemic.

While incoming Democratic governors in states like Ohio, Iowa, Georgia and Texas are unlikely to dismantle every parental notification or curriculum transparency law overnight, education battles in those states are poised to shift sharply — particularly around school choice, state takeovers, and public school funding.

Since the pandemic, contentious school board meetings have fueled a nationwide movement of parents demanding greater oversight of classroom instruction and challenging sexually explicit or LGBTQ-related books in school libraries.

DEMOCRATS SEIZE MAJORITY OF GOVERNORS’ OFFICES IN ELECTION-NIGHT SHIFT

Conservative groups capitalized on that momentum. Beginning in 2022, the Virginia-based American Principles Project (APP) entered local school board races in Florida, airing attack ads criticizing critical race theory and gender ideology. Alongside groups like the 1776 Project PAC, APP helped conservatives flip school board seats across Florida after Gov. Ron DeSantis broke precedent by actively endorsing local school board candidates who backed his pro-parent agenda.

Republican governors soon followed up with statewide legislation establishing "Parents' Bills of Rights" and curriculum transparency mandates:

FLORIDA'S DESANTIS DESCRIBES GOP MIDTERMS WIPEOUT AS 'CLOSE TO AN EXTINCTION-LEVEL EVENT' FOR REPUBLICANS

DEPT OF ED PUSHES AHEAD WITH EFFORTS TO DISMANTLE FEDERAL BUREAUCRACY AFTER BLUE WAVE

Now, voters in those four states have elected Democratic governors: Amy Acton in Ohio, Rob Sand in Iowa, Keisha Lance Bottoms in Georgia and Gina Hinojosa in Texas.

Even if those incoming governors want to roll back existing parental rights laws, several will face steep legislative hurdles. Acton, Sand and Bottoms will still contend with Republican-controlled legislatures capable of blocking repeals, though Democrats made legislative gains in Texas and Georgia during the midterms.

Notably, none of the four governors-elect campaigned explicitly on repealing their states' Parents' Bills of Rights. Instead, they largely sidestepped cultural flashpoints in favor of attacking GOP-backed private school voucher programs and calling for increased public school funding.

DEMOCRATS COULD CREATE 'ANGRY' 'SINGLE-ISSUE' VOTERS IN 2028 IF THEY REMOVE SCHOOL CHOICE, CEO WARNS

"This is a victory for the parents of Texas. We are taking our children’s education back from a government that has failed them," Hinojosa told supporters. "Schools will not be taken out of our control. They will not be shuttered or suffocated... On day one, I will fire [Texas Education Agency Commissioner] Mike Morath, and we will work tirelessly to repair the damage of the Texas voucher scam, and end an era in which our schools are sold for parts."

Their pushback comes as major urban districts navigate shifting enrollment dynamics. In February, for example, the Houston Independent School District's state-appointed board voted unanimously to close or consolidate 12 campuses ahead of the 2026–2027 school year, citing enrollment declines alongside the state's expanding school choice framework.

Still, conservatives warn that Hinojosa's legislative record signals a threat to parental protections in Texas.

During the campaign, Abbott's team ran ads featuring Moms for Liberty activist Denise Bell arguing that Hinojosa's policies would undermine parents and jeopardize fairness in girls' sports.

"Gina Hinojosa voted in favor of schools transitioning students behind parents’ backs, for sex change surgeries for kids, and for boys competing in girls’ sports—all radical policies that Governor Abbott has fought against time and again," Abbott’s campaign said in a statement accompanying the ad. "Parents should be the primary decision makers in their children’s lives."

Meanwhile, the Trump administration is signaling it will use federal leverage to keep parental rights policies intact regardless of statehouse flips. Last year, President Donald Trump signed executive orders tying federal education funding to strict anti-discrimination compliance and prohibiting diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) programs in schools.

Following the midterm results, the U.S. Department of Education told Fox News Digital it plans to escalate enforcement — including investigating school districts accused of concealing a student's gender transition from parents.

"The Department will double down on its efforts to restore parental rights, return education to the states, and open more higher education pathways for students," an Education Department spokesperson told Fox News Digital.

TEXAS DEMOCRATS PUT DEI BACK ON AGENDA AFTER SWEEPING TO POWER

Defending Education, which has been the tip of the spear of the parental rights movement, investigating civil rights violations and exposing far-left elements of curriculum across the country, told Fox News Digital that the federal government already has strong laws, like FERPA and the Protection of Pupil Rights Amendment (PPRA), to protect parental rights.

"These give the administration solid footing to make sure parents aren’t being kept in the dark about what’s happening at school, can review curriculum, and can opt out of invasive surveys on topics like gender ideology," said Paul Runko, senior director of strategic initiatives at Defending Education.

He added: "The Justice Department has also stepped up, using investigations and lawsuits to push back against state and local school boards that cross the line."

Runko explained further that civil rights protections would allow parents to continue to speak out in public forums.

"On top of that, the First and 14th Amendments protect a parent’s right to speak up and decide how to raise their children. Recent federal court wins by parents in Ohio, Maryland and California send a clear message that school districts should think twice about ignoring parental rights," he said.

None of the newly elected governors responded to Fox News Digital's requests for comment.

item.title: Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson faces audit calls after CFO quits over 'financial integrity' concerns
item.description: Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson faces fresh budget turmoil after CFO Ashlee Gabrysch abruptly resigns, questioning the city's financial reporting and budget calculations.
item.content:encoded:
Chicago’s chief financial officer, who formerly worked for a top credit ratings bureau, resigned Friday citing financial integrity concerns, casting a shadow over the fiscal management of progressive Mayor Brandon Johnson amid a fight over the FY-2027 budget.

Chicago CFO Ashlee Gabrysch served only three months before the onetime Fitch Ratings executive stepped down, saying she could no longer meet her professional obligations under the conditions of her employment, according to a resignation letter obtained by the Chicago Tribune. 

"The chief financial officer’s statements about the city’s finances are relied upon by investors, rating agencies, City Council, and taxpayers, and they must be complete and accurate," Gabrysch wrote, according to the Tribune.

"I am not able to fulfill those obligations under the conditions in which I have been asked to serve."

Johnson did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment, but his press secretary accused Gabrysch of being "largely absent" during key parts of the next budget’s creation process.

CHICAGO MAYOR CALLS ICE RAIDS ‘TERRORISM,’ SAYS TRUMP'S AMERICA APPEARS AS ‘IF THE CONFEDERACY WON’

The mayor's office also accused Gabrysch of improperly directing a $75 million payment to city pension funds before the required legal procedures had been completed, saying it would refer the matter to Chicago's Office of Inspector General for review.

The Tribune recounted recent events in the budget process involving Gabrysch, including that she disagreed with Johnson over assertions about the size of the city’s deficit.

In September, Johnson announced that the Windy City faces a projected $882 million budget shortfall in 2027, which local media described as smaller than a typical election year and lighter than the $1.15 billion deficit projected in 2025. The city holds its elections in odd years.

"We have difficult and consequential decisions ahead of us as we work to address the structural financial challenges that have confronted Chicago for decades," Johnson said at the time, according to Chicago’s PBS affiliate.

However, according to the Tribune, Johnson claimed the true figure is now $662 million, "adjusted" in concert with planned borrowing to help fund settlement amounts involving police officers.

CHICAGO MAYOR CALLS DOGE AN ‘ACT OF WAR’

Gabrysch challenged that accounting during budget hearings, arguing that the settlement expenses should remain part of the deficit and that borrowing to pay them amounted to a temporary fix rather than a lasting solution.

While the administration maintained that 76% of its budget measures addressed underlying financial problems, Gabrysch calculated the figure at just 56%, according to the Tribune.

Alderman Marty Quinn, D-Midway, questioned Johnson’s handling at the time, according to the paper, saying he was "not surprised that the mayor may be a little disingenuous here, that seems to be his normal course."

Gabrysch also stopped short of calling Johnson's proposed $17.6 billion budget balanced during an October City Council hearing, arguing that the city needed to demonstrate progress toward reducing future deficits, according to Crain's Chicago Business.

City Comptroller Michael Belsky maintained that proposed revenues matched expenditures, while acting Budget Director Jonathan Ernst defended the administration's calculations and its plan to borrow roughly $480 million to cover legal settlements.

Gabrysch warned that the city anticipated issuing $350 million in settlement-related bonds in 2027, with an estimated $190 million in interest costs over seven years, according to Crain's.

Her resignation prompted Council Finance Committee chairman Pat Dowell, D-South Loop, to call for an independent audit.

The departure adds to a wave of turnover in Johnson's financial leadership, including two previous CFO departures this year and the resignation of the city's budget director in August. The upheaval comes as Chicago grapples with mounting financial obligations and credit-rating downgrades.

The collision between a cruise ship and tanker caused the passenger vessel to take on water before capsizing around 22 minutes later, which sent passengers and crew scrambling to get off the ship. The Atlantic Asphalt, which carried 19 crew members and a local river pilot, departed from Lower 9 Mile Anchorage, located near Mississippi River mile marker 83.

Its destination was an oil facility in Reserve, Louisiana.

According to the NTSB, the tanker suffered a steering casualty which left its rudder fixed in the starboard position, causing the vessel to make a turn toward the Mississippi River's east bank.

It's not yet clear what caused the steering malfunction.

According to the NTSB, crew on the tanker issued various emergency commands such as a whistle, requests for assistance, commands to deploy anchors, emergency orders and radio warnings before colliding with the American Heritage.
